subject: Private deployment - Operational ownership and commingling controls Q&A
messages:
From: John Ortega <j.ortega@stellarishealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Park <alyssa@stellarishealth.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on operator ownership and data commingling for private deployment

Ben / team,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our procurement and security teams are reviewing the RFP response and we have a couple of follow-ups specifically around operational ownership and commingling controls for a VPC/on-prem deployment: 

- Who is responsible for operator accounts and day-to-day operator activities (customer ops vs Redwood SRE) after handoff?
- For on-prem installs, can you confirm whether any multi-tenant services (e.g., monitoring, metrics, health checks) phone home to Redwood by default? If so, can that be disabled?
- If we run multiple Stellaris environments in a single physical cluster, how do you prevent cross-tenant inference data commingling at rest and in logs?

We'd like brief, interview-style answers we can include in our compliance packet. If you need to include attachments or an ownership matrix, that would be helpful.

Thanks,
John Ortega
Director, IT Procurement
Stellaris Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: John Ortega <j.ortega@stellarishealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Mar 2028 12:06:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Questions on operator ownership and data commingling for private deployment

John — appreciate the clear list. Short answers first, then I'll loop in Laura for the technical evidence pack.

1) Operator ownership: Customer owns operators post-handoff. Redwood provides an operator runbook, an onboarding/transfer window (2 weeks), and optional managed-ops add-on (SLA'd) if you want Redwood to retain operator responsibilities. The default commercial model for private (on-prem/VPC) is customer-operated.

2) Phone-home behavior: By default the private deployment does not phone home for inference or telemetry. There is an optional telemetry agent used during onboarding that can be enabled; it is off by default and must be explicitly authorized. Health checks run locally. Optional status reporting to Redwood is available as an opt-in webhook that can be configured to point at a firewall-proxied endpoint.

3) Data commingling: For on-prem/VPC installs using a single cluster for multiple Stellaris environments, we enforce strict tenancy via namespace isolation, KMS key scoping per-tenant, and drive mount isolation. Our runtime writes customer artifacts to tenant-scoped volumes and segregates logs using tenant identifiers; by default we do not write tokens or request payloads to centralized Redwood services. Access controls are enforced via kube RBAC and platform-level ACLs.

I'll attach our operator responsibilities matrix and a short checklist for evidence we can provide. Laura will add more technical detail and sample artifacts (S3/Netflow screenshots, KMS key binding examples).

Next step: Laura to share the two artifacts by end of day tomorrow. If procurement needs a redline to the contract for the managed-ops optionality, loop Marissa and I'll coordinate.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: John Ortega <j.ortega@stellarishealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Mar 2028 15:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Questions on operator ownership and data commingling for private deployment

John — adding the technical artifacts we discussed. Attached: operator-responsibilities matrix (PDF) and a network/evidence checklist (XLSX). Highlights below and a compact Q&A to include in your packet.

Attachment highlights:
- redwood-operator-responsibilities.pdf: Ownership table (pre-handoff, handoff window, post-handoff) showing specific tasks (patching, key rotation, incident triage, backups) and who performs them. Optional managed-ops tasks are marked.
- network-evidence-checklist.xlsx: Template you can use to capture network diagrams, KMS key IDs, mount points, and audit log snippets.

Compact Q&A (suitable for inclusion):
- Operator accounts: Created by customer during install; Redwood recommends least-privilege operator role and provides CLI + systemd unit examples. We hand over access within the two-week transfer window and perform one paired runbook walkthrough.
- Telemetry: No automatic outbound inference telemetry. Optional onboarding telemetry agent collects anonymized metrics (CPU/mem/util) only and must be enabled by customer.
- Log handling: Runtime emits structured logs to stdout; customers configure log collectors (Fluentd/Vector) to ship logs to tenant-scoped destinations. We provide sample Fluentd config that tags records with tenant_id.
- KMS: Customer-managed KMS recommended. If Redwood-run KMS is used (rare), keys are tenant-scoped and access is restricted to the Redwood process; attestation artifacts can be provided.

Evidence we can provide on request (samples): sample Fluentd config, KMS binding JSON (sanitized), example audit log snippet, and a runbook excerpt. If you want these embedded into the RFP packet, say which items to sanitize.

Attachments: redwood-operator-responsibilities.pdf (4 pages), network-evidence-checklist.xlsx

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: procurement@stellarishealth.com
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 13 Mar 2028 21:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on operator ownership and data commingling for private deployment

Ben / Laura — thanks for the quick, concrete responses and for the attachments. Procurement reviewed the operator responsibilities pdf and the checklist; both look useful. A few follow-ups before we include in the compliance packet:

- Can you provide an example Fluentd config sanitized for production (remove IPs/usernames)?
- Please confirm that the optional telemetry agent can be fully disabled via a single flag in the installer and that no outbound connections occur when disabled.
- For the KMS examples, please provide sanitized key IDs and a short note on rotation frequency recommendations.

If you can drop those three items (Fluentd sample, installer flag confirmation, KMS note) into the Drive folder linked here, we should be able to move to legal for a draft SOW. Doc link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-evidence

Thanks — procurement team
Stellaris Health
